attempted_claim: Let Z-plus be the semi-Fano 3-fold obtained as the blow-up of P^3 along a smooth complete-intersection curve of type (2,3) with anticanonical K3 divisor Sigma-plus of Picard rank 2, and Z-minus be the semi-Fano 3-fold obtained as the blow-up of the smooth quadric Q^3 along a smooth conic with anticanonical K3 divisor Sigma-minus, each equipped with the Nordstrom extra-twisted involution tau-plus/tau-minus acting non-symplectically on the K3 with isolated fixed points plus a fixed curve as specified by the Brandhorst fixed-lattice data. Does there exist a hyper-Kahler rotation r: Sigma-plus -> Sigma-minus intertwining tau-plus with tau-minus and realizing extra-twisted gluing angle pi/2 in orthogonal configuration, hence a closed extra-twisted connected sum 7-manifold with exponentially small torsion from this pair? A complete answer is either an explicit lattice-polarized matching r with intersection-matrix verification and resulting glued closed G2 3-form, or a proof that no such r exists via Nikulin lattice-embedding or fixed-locus incompatibility identifying the precise matching obstruction.

Each has weaker hypotheses (any K3, any block) and jointly implies no tau as specified and hence no intertwining r, without needing the pair-specific N+- computation.
